mainTopic: Two sources for rejecting a משומד's קרבן, the meaning of 'בהמה' said about people, and רבן גמליאל's ban on the שחיטה of a כותי.
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from 'מעם הארץ' that a משומד cannot bring a קרבן. In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון learns this from a different phrase, and רב המנונא shows where the two views differ. Since an earlier source on the דף ('מכם') already excluded a משומד, the גמרא explains that one source is about a חטאת and the other about an עולה, and shows why both are needed. Next, the גמרא asks whether calling people 'בהמה' always means a weakness, and it carefully separates 'בהמה' alone, 'אדם ובהמה' together, and the two separate groups in ירמיהו. Then a new topic begins: רבן גמליאל's בית דין voted to forbid the שחיטה of a כותי. רבי יעקב בר אידי insists the ban covers even a כותי watched by a Jew, and the גמרא asks if רבי זירא agreed. A story about רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי eating a כותי's שחיטה leads רבי זירא to conclude that they knew the ban and did not accept it, since ה׳ protects צדיקים from eating forbidden food by mistake.

steps.title: A second source excludes the משומד from bringing a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'מעם הארץ' that a משומד cannot bring a קרבן. This seems to repeat what the earlier source on the דף already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of the common people' (ויקרא 4:27) comes to exclude a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that learns from the words 'מעם הארץ' that a משומד does not bring a sin offering. It is setting up a problem, because the daf already had a different source for this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, the words 'מכם, ולא כולכם' were used to exclude a משומד from bringing a קרבן. Now a second פסוק is used for the same exclusion. The תורה does not normally teach the same thing twice, so we need to know why there are two sources.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who deliberately and habitually breaks a Torah law; a transgressor
To exclude; except for
Here, literally 'the people of the land,' meaning an ordinary Jew in the פסוק about a sin offering

phrases.english: 'Of the common people'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27, the פסוק about an ordinary person who sins by accident and brings a חטאת.

phrases.english: excludes a transgressor.
phrases.notes: The word 'מ' (from) means 'some of' the people, not all of them, so the משומד is left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second derivation that seems to duplicate the earlier source (מכם, ולא כולכם) from earlier on the דף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier source that already excluded a משומד from bringing a קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one פסוק already excludes the משומד, why would another פסוק be needed for the same exclusion?

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only someone who would repent can bring an offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם' that only a person who would stop sinning if he knew can bring a קרבן for an accidental sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוסי says in the name of רבי שמעון: 'that may not be done, unwittingly, and he becomes guilty.' A person who would turn back once he knows brings a קרבן for his accidental sin. A person who would not turn back once he knows does not bring a קרבן for his accidental sin.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון learns the exclusion of a משומד from a different phrase. He makes it depend on whether the person would stop sinning if he knew it was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, a קרבן fixes a real accident, meaning a sin the person would have avoided had he known. Someone who would sin anyway is not really sinning 'by accident,' so he cannot bring a חטאת. The test is about the specific sin, not about the person in general.

keyTerms.meaning: An accidental, unknowing sin
One who would turn back (stop) once he knows the act is forbidden
An offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
'that may not be done, unwittingly, and he becomes guilty,'
one who turns back because of his knowledge
phrases.notes: He means someone who would stop if he found out the act is forbidden.

phrases.english: brings an offering for his accidental sin;
one who does not turn back because of his knowledge
does not bring an offering for his accidental sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק and a different test for excluding the משומד, in contrast to the first view in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a person who would stop if he knew the act was forbidden can bring a קרבן for his accidental sin.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the first view and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two views in the ברייתא actually lead to different results. This sets up רב המנונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views exclude a משומד, so at first they seem to say the same thing. The question pushes us to find a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: And we said: What is between them?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is recalling a discussion it had elsewhere about this same ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two derivations just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the first view and רבי שמעון would rule differently.

steps.title: רב המנונא: a משומד for חלב who brings an offering for blood
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says the views differ about a person who is a משומד only for eating חלב and brings a קרבן for accidentally eating blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב המנונא said: A person who is a משומד for eating חלב and brings an offering for blood is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives the case where the two views split: a משומד for one sin who wants to bring a קרבן for a different sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first view, he is a משומד, so his קרבן is not accepted at all. For רבי שמעון, the test is about the specific sin. He would stop eating blood if he knew, so he can bring a קרבן for the blood. This shows that both views really do exclude a משומד, which brings back the question of why two sources are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fats of a domesticated animal
Blood, which is forbidden to eat
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון accepts a קרבן from a משומד for the same sin he does on purpose. He only accepts a קרבן for a different sin, one the person would avoid if he knew.

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:
A transgressor regarding eating forbidden fat
who brought an offering for eating blood
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא מְשׁוּמָּד לֶאֱכוֹל חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a specific case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A משומד for חלב who brings a קרבן for accidentally eating blood: rejected by the first view, accepted by רבי שמעון.

steps.title: One source is for a sin offering, one for a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the double-source problem: one פסוק excludes the משומד from a חטאת, and the other excludes him from an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about a חטאת, and one is about an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash between the two sources by saying each one teaches about a different type of קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מעם הארץ' appears in the section about the חטאת, so it excludes a משומד from bringing a sin offering. The earlier source, 'מכם,' teaches the same rule for an עולה. So neither source is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering, brought to atone for an accidental sin
Burnt offering, completely burned on the מזבח
One ... and one

phrases.english: One is about a sin offering, and one is about a burnt offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 1 about having two sources for the same exclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: each covers a different type of קרבן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to teach the same exclusion, so one looked unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source excludes the משומד from a חטאת, and the other excludes him from an עולה.

steps.title: Why both sources are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we could not learn the עולה from the חטאת or the חטאת from the עולה, so both sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the Torah only taught us about a חטאת, we would say it is rejected because it brings atonement, but an עולה is a gift, so we should accept it from him. And if the Torah only taught us about an עולה, we would say it is rejected because it is not an obligation, but a חטאת is an obligation, so we should accept it from him. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a צריכותא: it shows that each source has a reason that would not carry over to the other kind of קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת brings atonement, and a משומד might not deserve atonement. An עולה is just a gift, so maybe a gift would be accepted even from him. On the other hand, an עולה is voluntary, so rejecting it is easy. A חטאת is required, so maybe we would let him fulfill his obligation. Since each reasoning could go either way, the Torah had to teach both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both sources are needed)
Atonement
A gift
An obligation
I might say (I would have thought)

steps.whatToRemember: A משומד's קרבן is rejected both for a חטאת ('מעם הארץ') and for an עולה ('מכם'). We need two sources because a חטאת is for atonement but required, while an עולה is a gift but voluntary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכותא: when the Torah seems to repeat itself, the גמרא shows that each case has its own reason that could not be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And both are needed, for if it had taught us only a sin offering,
it is because it is for atonement,
phrases.notes: We would think the חטאת is rejected because a משומד does not deserve atonement.

phrases.english: but a burnt offering, which is a gift,
I would say to accept it from him.
And if it had taught us only a burnt offering,
it is because it is not an obligation,
but a sin offering, which is an obligation,
I would say to accept it from him,
so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies the answer of step 5 by showing that neither source could be learned from the other.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both exclusions are needed: a חטאת and an עולה each have a reason that might have allowed accepting them from a משומד, so the Torah teaches the rejection for each separately.

steps.title: Does 'animal' always mean something negative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that calling people בהמה shows a weakness, using a פסוק in תהלים that רב reads as praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that every time the word 'animal' is written about people, it means a weakness? But a פסוק says 'Man and animal You save, ה׳‎.' רב explained that these are smart people who act humbly, like an animal. That is praise, not a weakness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the earlier idea that 'people like a בהמה' means people with a weakness. It brings a פסוק where 'animal' describes people in a good way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא used מן הבהמה to include people who are 'like animals,' which sounds like a weakness. רב reads אדם ובהמה תושיע ה׳ as praise for clever people who humble themselves. So 'animal' cannot always mean something negative.

keyTerms.meaning: A weakness or lower level
Clever and sharp in their thinking
They act humbly, like a simple animal

phrases.english: And everywhere that 'animal' is written,
is it a weakness?
But isn't it written: 'Man and animal You save, ה׳,'
and Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁהֵן עֲרוּמִין בְּדַעַת,
phrases.english: These are people who are clever in their minds,
and make themselves like an animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בְּהֵמָה, גְּרִיעוּתָא הִיא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the double-source discussion to the meaning of 'like a בהמה' in the earlier ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'בהמה' said about people always shows a weakness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק uses 'בהמה' for people, and רב reads it as praise, so the word cannot always be negative.

steps.title: Animal alone versus man and animal together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in תהלים both words appear together, while in our פסוק 'animal' appears by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: There the פסוק says 'man and animal.' Here only 'animal' is written by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a difference in wording between the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אדם and בהמה come together, it describes someone with a person's brains and an animal's humility, which is praise. When בהמה stands alone, it points only to the animal side, which is a weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, alone
There... here (comparing two cases)

phrases.english: There it is written 'man and animal';
here 'animal' alone is written.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the wording of the two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of 'בהמה' for people should mean the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'בהמה' by itself shows a weakness; 'אדם ובהמה' together is praise.

steps.title: Is 'man and animal' together always praise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule with a פסוק in ירמיהו where 'seed of man and seed of animal' appear together, but the 'animal' part is not praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that every time 'man and animal' are written together, it is praise? But a פסוק says 'I will sow the house of Israel with the seed of man and the seed of animal'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer it just gave. It brings a פסוק where 'man' and 'animal' appear together, but the 'animal' side does not seem to be praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said that 'אדם ובהמה' together means something good. In ירמיהו both words appear, yet 'seed of animal' is understood as the simpler, lower people. So the rule from step 8 seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: A good quality, praise
'Seed of animal,' understood as the simpler, lower group of people

phrases.english: And everywhere that 'man and animal' is written,
is it praise?
But isn't it written: 'And I will sow the house of Israel
with the seed of man and the seed of animal'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'אדם ובהמה' together always means praise.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ירמיהו both words appear together, but the 'animal' side is not praise.

steps.title: The פסוק in ירמיהו separates the two groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ירמיהו splits 'seed of man' and 'seed of animal' into two separate groups, so it is not one combined description.
steps.simpleTranslation: There the פסוק itself separates them: 'seed of man' is one group, and 'seed of animal' is a different group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second question by showing that the פסוק in ירמיהו is not really 'man and animal' joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תהלים, 'אדם ובהמה' describes one kind of person with both qualities. In ירמיהו, the repeated word 'זרע' splits them into two different groups. So the 'animal' group there stands alone, and the rule from step 8 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק divided them
Separate, on its own

steps.whatToRemember: 'בהמה' alone about people shows a weakness. 'אדם ובהמה' joined in one description is praise. When the פסוק separates them, as in ירמיהו, the 'animal' group again stands on its own.

phrases.english: There, doesn't the verse divide them?
phrases.notes: The word 'seed' is repeated before each group, which is what splits them apart.

phrases.english: 'Seed of man' is separate,
and 'seed of animal' is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and closes the discussion about the word 'בהמה.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the wording of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any time both words appear in a פסוק, they form one praised description.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only when the two words describe one person together is it praise. In ירמיהו they are two separate groups.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's court forbade the שחיטה of a כותי
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign for the sages' names, a chain of sages reports that רבן גמליאל and his בית דין voted and forbade meat slaughtered by a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: נקל״ף.) רבי חנן said, in the name of רבי יעקב בר אידי, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of בר קפרא: רבן גמליאל and his court voted about the שחיטה of a כותי, and they forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic, the שחיטה of a כותי. It gives a ruling from רבן גמליאל's בית דין, passed down through a chain of sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The memory sign helps the learner remember the chain of names: נ for חנן, ק for יעקב, ל for לוי, and פ for קפרא. The ruling itself is that a formal vote of the court forbade meat slaughtered by a כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign made of letters to help remember names
They counted votes, decided by a vote
Slaughter done by a כותי
And they forbade it

phrases.english: (Memory sign: נקל״ף.)
phrases.notes: Each letter hints at one name in the chain below: חנן, יעקב, לוי, קפרא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanan said that Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Bar Kappara:
Rabban Gamliel and his court
voted about the slaughter of a Kuti
and they forbade it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the word 'בהמה' ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and his בית דין voted to forbid meat slaughtered by a כותי.

steps.title: Maybe the ban is only when no Jew is watching
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests that the ruling may only forbid a כותי's שחיטה when no Jew is standing over him to supervise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי יעקב בר אידי: Maybe the רבי only heard this ruling about a case where no Jew is standing over the כותי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks whether the ban is narrower than it sounds. He suggests it might only apply when no Jew is supervising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Jew watches the כותי slaughter, we could check that it was done properly. So רבי זירא suggests the ban might only cover the unsupervised case. That would make the ruling much narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
Standing over him, supervising him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi:
Perhaps the Rabbi heard it only
phrases.notes: 'The רבי' means the teacher who passed this ruling down.

phrases.english: where no Jew is standing over him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how far the ruling in step 11 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban cover even a supervised שחיטה, or only an unsupervised one?

steps.title: The unsupervised case is too obvious to need a ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי rejects רבי זירא's suggestion sharply. Of course a כותי's שחיטה with no Jew watching is forbidden, so the court's vote must have been about the supervised case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: This scholar seems like someone who never learned the teaching! When no Jew is standing over him, does that even need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי rejects the narrow reading. A vote by the court would not be needed for something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding an unsupervised כותי's שחיטה is so obvious that no court would need to vote on it. So the vote must have forbidden the שחיטה even when a Jew is standing over him. This makes the ban much wider than רבי זירא suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling that was learned
They learned, they studied
Does it need to be said? (meaning: it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying the unsupervised case is allowed. He means it is so clearly forbidden that the court's vote must be about the harder case, where a Jew is watching.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יעקב בר אידי, רבן גמליאל's court forbade a כותי's שחיטה even when a Jew is supervising.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one of the Rabbis seems
like people who have not learned the teaching!
When no Jew is standing over him,
does it need to be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּמֵי הַאי מֵרַבָּנַן כִּדְלָא גְּמִירִי אִינָשֵׁי שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's narrow reading from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ban only covers an unsupervised כותי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The unsupervised case is too obvious to need a vote by the court, so the ruling must reach the supervised case too.

steps.title: Did רבי זירא accept the rejection?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא accepted רבי יעקב בר אידי's rejection of his suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי זירא accept this answer from רבי יעקב בר אידי, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא agreed with the sharp rejection he just heard. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רבי יעקב בר אידי said the ban must cover even a כותי who is being watched by a Jew. Now we want to know whether רבי זירא gave up his own idea and agreed. The answer will tell us how רבי זירא understood the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it from him (agreed with his answer)

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא, and "him" is רבי יעקב בר אידי, who rejected his idea in step 13.

phrases.english: or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ אוֹ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי זירא reacted to the rejection in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי זירא agreed that the ban covers even a supervised כותי.

steps.title: Report that רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי ate a כותי's slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports that he saw רבי יוחנן eat meat slaughtered by a כותי, and רבי אסי ate it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב נחמן בר יצחק said in the name of רבי אסי: "I saw רבי יוחנן eat from a כותי's slaughter." רבי אסי also ate from a כותי's slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof with a story about two great sages who ate meat slaughtered by a כותי. This story sets up what רבי זירא will say about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems strange, because step 11 said רבן גמליאל's court banned this meat. The proof will depend on how רבי זירא explains why these sages ate it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal slaughtered by a כותי

phrases.english: Come and hear
for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
that Rabbi Asi said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan
eat from the slaughter of a Kuti.
Rabbi Asi too
ate from the slaughter of a Kuti.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that will be used to answer the question in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי זירא accepted רבי יעקב בר אידי's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אסי's report about רבי יוחנן and himself.

steps.title: רבי זירא wonders why they ate it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether these sages never heard of the ban, or heard it and did not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא wondered: maybe they never heard of the ban, and if they had heard it they would have accepted it? Or maybe they did hear it and did not accept it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is puzzled about why רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי ate this meat. He lays out two possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one is that they simply did not know about רבן גמליאל's ban. Option two is that they knew about it and disagreed with it. Notice that רבי זירא does not offer a third option, that they ate from a supervised כותי. That missing option is the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Wondered, was puzzled
They heard it (knew of the ruling)
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי זירא is asking about the ban in general. The point is that he never says "maybe they ate from a supervised כותי." That suggests he now agrees the ban covers even the supervised case.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira wondered about it:
Did they not hear it,
so that if they had heard it
they would have accepted it,
or perhaps they heard it
and did not accept it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי זירא's reaction to the story in step 15. His reaction is the actual proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי ate a כותי's slaughter despite the court's ban.

steps.title: רבי זירא decides they heard it and rejected it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא concludes that the sages knew of the ban and did not accept it. Otherwise they would have been led to eat forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא then answered his own question: It makes sense that they heard it and did not accept it. If you think they never heard it, and would have accepted it if they had, how could they have ended up eating forbidden food?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers his own question. He says the sages must have known about the ban and disagreed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had not known the ban, they would have been eating truly forbidden food by mistake. רבי זירא finds that hard to believe about such great people. So they must have held that the meat was permitted, because they did not accept the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolved it for himself, answered his own question
It stands to reason, it makes sense
Forbidden food

phrases.english: He then resolved it for himself:
It stands to reason that they heard it
and did not accept it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ
phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that they did not hear it,
and that if they had heard it
they would have accepted it,
how would the matter have come about
for them to eat forbidden food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's own question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They knew of the ban and did not accept it, because righteous people would not be led to eat forbidden food by mistake.

steps.title: Righteous people are protected from mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא supports his answer with a קל וחומר‎. ה׳ does not bring mishaps even through the animals of the righteous, so surely not through the righteous themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if ה׳ does not bring a mishap even through the animals of righteous people, then surely He does not bring one through the righteous people themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא backs up his reasoning with a קל וחומר about how ה׳ protects the righteous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a צדיק's animal is kept from causing a wrong, then a צדיק himself will surely be kept from eating forbidden food. So רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי could not have been eating by mistake; they truly held the meat was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Righteous people
A mishap, a stumbling into wrongdoing
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא explains that רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי knowingly rejected רבן גמליאל's ban. He does not say "they ate from a supervised כותי," which suggests he agreed that the ban covers even that case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that ה׳ protects צדיקים from accidentally sinning, becomes a tool for working out what great sages actually held.

phrases.english: Now, through the animals of the righteous
the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
bring a mishap through them;
the righteous themselves,
is it not all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי זירא's conclusion in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That righteous sages would not eat forbidden food by mistake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from ה׳ protecting even the animals of צדיקים.
